Both implementations gate the real work behind `if (i != -23) ...` / `if (i != -23) return false` - i.e. every real caller is expected to pass the literal `-23`, making `i` an opcode/tag-style decoy param rather than meaningful data. Returns whether the unlock/unmap actually happened.

Interface method implemented by `D3dIndexBuffer` (releases the native `IDirect3DIndexBuffer` and zeroes size fields) and `GlIndexBufferArb` (delegates to the GL buffer-object release, but only when `i == 23315` - the opposite polarity of D3D's `if (i != 23315) method23(65, -35)` extra-resize branch). The two implementations disagree on how `i` gates behaviour, reinforcing that it's a decoy/tag param expected to carry one specific sentinel value (23315) at real call sites rather than meaningful data - dispose/free the underlying native index buffer.

Interface method implemented by `D3dIndexBuffer` and `GlIndexBufferArb`. Both multiply `indexCount` by the element size from the buffer's `MovementDirection`-typed format field (`aMovementDirection_..!!.anInt1178`) to compute a byte size, and (re)allocate the native/GL buffer only when the new size exceeds the previously allocated size - i.e. lazily grows the index buffer to hold at least `indexCount` indices. `i` is discarded except for a dead `anInt8516 = -78/118` decoy write in the D3D implementation.

Interface method implemented by `D3dIndexBuffer` (calls `Lock(0, size, flags, sharedGeometryBuffer)`) and `GlIndexBufferArb` (delegates to the GL buffer-object map helper `super.method2120`). Returns the mapped `Buffer` to write indices into, or null on failure. In the D3D impl, `ensureResized` (2nd param) triggers a `method23(-111, 54)` capacity-check call first, and `discardExisting` (1st param) is AND-ed with an internal 'dynamic buffer' flag to pick the D3D lock-discard flag (8192) vs 0.

Interface method implemented by `D3dIndexBuffer` and `GlIndexBufferArb`. Both simply return the buffer's `MovementDirection`-typed format field (despite the type's name, in this context it represents the index element format/primitive type set at construction), with a decoy `if (i <= 19) <unrelated static> = null` side effect in both implementations gated on the byte param - real call sites were not enumerated in this pass, so the exact sentinel value expected is unconfirmed.
